verdict.rationale: Sumsub documents a RESTful API for processing applicant data and documents, and says it gives developers full control over the verification flow, including generating access tokens for SDK sessions. So the core of driving verification through the API is first-party. However, the evidence never shows the individual lifecycle endpoints, and no OpenAPI spec was found (all probed paths returned 404). missing for 10: documented status-retrieval endpoint, results and captured-media retrieval endpoints, cancel/reset endpoint, redaction/deletion endpoint, per-step API reference evidence, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the whole verification lifecycle is drivable through the API — create a session, get its status, retrieve results and captured media, and cancel or redact it — with every step documented

citations.quote: With the Sumsub API, you can process the applicant data and documents submitted for verification through simple RESTful APIs.
The Sumsub API lets you integrate identity verification directly into your product, giving you full control over the verification flow
Generate an access token to be passed to the WebSDK during initialization.
